title: Spinach and Mascarpone Pilas Burekas Pie
subtitle: with slow-cooked black spinach
description: A coiled burekas-style pie of stretched pilas dough rolled around slow-cooked black spinach and mascarpone. The dough needs a night in the fridge, and the recipe makes more dough than needed in case some sheets tear.

steps.text: Make the dough: mix the flour, 1 tsp salt, 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, vinegar, vodka and water in a mixer with a dough hook on medium speed for about 7 minutes until smooth and slightly sticky.

Divide the dough into 10 balls of about 60 g each. Arrange them in a container about 2 cm apart. Add olive oil to half the height of the balls, cover and refrigerate for 12 hours (the dough needs the rest or it will tear).
Make the filling: wilt 1 kg of the spinach in a wide pot with no oil or liquid over low heat for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally, as it releases liquid and cooks in it.
Add 1 cup vegetable oil and cook for about 1 1/2 hours until the spinach turns black and has a bitter-sweet flavour. Season with salt and pepper, stir and cool.
Preheat the oven to 220°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Mix the cooked spinach with the mascarpone and adjust the seasoning.

Chop the remaining raw spinach and mix it with the cooked spinach and mascarpone mixture. Take a dough ball out of the oil and stretch it gently with shaking motions to loosen it. Place on a work surface and carefully but firmly stretch it into a rectangle as thin as possible. The dough should be taut and transparent; a few small holes are fine.

Spread about 1/6 of the filling along one long side of the dough so a strip covers about 1/3 of the surface. Roll tightly from the filled side to the opposite side. Place in the centre of the tray and coil into a snail.
Stretch and fill 5 more dough balls the same way, coiling each filled roll around the central snail.
Brush the pie with olive oil and bake for 25-30 minutes until the top is browned.
